prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "build", with the standing line "The folder of platform templates and icons that wails build fills with your project's details to produce a shippable app." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A shallow three-compartment wooden tray, its front edge lettered build, standing on a workbench. A card of project details (product name, version, copyright, company) is pressed down through two stencil-like sheets lying in the compartments — one sheet in the darwin compartment, one in the windows compartment. Two filled paths leave the tray: the darwin path carries a finished macOS app bundle, the windows path carries an installer, and both slide into the third compartment, bin. A short return loop shows a discarded sheet coming back into the tray as a fresh default.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one, a blank field in the stencil receiving the product name, the same card feeding both platforms. circle two, an empty icon slot beside a source picture being redrawn into an application icon. circle three, two nearly identical plist sheets, the dev copy carrying one extra allowance for local networking. circle four, a file properties panel showing company, description and copyright read back from the version details.

Colour is used so that Ochre marks project details being substituted into a template. Blue marks the macOS path. Vermilion marks the Windows installer path.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: three compartments in the tray, two plist variants, two supported architectures, four installer pages, two shortcuts created, macOS 10.13 minimum, Windows 10 minimum.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: build on the tray, darwin and windows on the two stencil compartments, bin on the output compartment, wails build and wails dev on the two presses, Info.plist on the macOS template sheet.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: build, darwin, windows, bin, wails build, wails dev, project details, app bundle, installer Info.plist, dev copy, local networking, icon slot, file properties welcome, choose folder, copy files, finish, runtime check desktop shortcut, start menu, uninstaller, file associations, custom protocols delete to restore, default files return, two architectures, Windows 10 minimum, macOS 10.13 minimum

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Templates hold blanks until a build fills them; bin receives every finished artefact One plist for release, one for development; a missing icon is regenerated from the source picture The installer checks architecture before copying anything; a browser runtime is installed first if absent Uninstalling removes shortcuts and registry entry Edited files are yours until deleted
